exhibits.title: The Frozen Tapestry and Its Thin Correction
exhibits.text:
A vast tapestry hangs the full height of the hall, its every thread already woven at ruinous cost in the arts below. This is W — a trained weight matrix, say of size d x d = 1000 x 1000 = 1,000,000 threads. The old way of attunement was to reweave the whole cloth: full fine-tuning learns an update matrix DELTA-W of the SAME shape as W (another 1,000,000 numbers), then hangs the new cloth W_new = W + DELTA-W in place of the old. For a work with hundreds of such matrices that is billions of threads to relearn and to store, and every adapted copy is as heavy as the original.

LoRA makes a different wager. It does not touch the great tapestry at all. The tapestry is FROZEN — no thread of W is ever pulled. Instead a thin, luminous correction is laid OVER it, and only that correction is learned.

The wager is this: the meaningful UPDATE does not need to be full-rank. DELTA-W can be approximated by the product of two thin matrices,

    DELTA-W  ~=  B . A

with an inner rank r (take r = 8). Then A is r x d = 8 x 1000, and B is d x r = 1000 x 8. Count the threads you must actually learn:

    full DELTA-W:  1000 x 1000            = 1,000,000
    B . A:         (1000 x 8) + (8 x 1000) =    16,000

Sixty-two times fewer. And because B . A multiplies out to a d x d array — the same 1000 x 1000 shape as DELTA-W — it slots straight into the seam:

    W_new  =  W + B . A

W stays frozen; only A and B are trained. That is the whole of LoRA, and the whole reason this wing exists.

exhibits.title: The Low-Rank Bet
exhibits.text:
Why should the update be allowed to be low-rank at all? Because of an empirical truth about fine-tuning: when you bend an already-trained model toward a new task, the change it needs is small and directed. It does not rewrite the model's whole understanding — it nudges it along a handful of directions. In the language of matrices, the meaningful part of DELTA-W lives in a SMALL SUBSPACE: a few strong directions carry almost all of the correction, and the rest is near-nothing.

A matrix whose action is concentrated in r directions HAS rank r. So writing DELTA-W ~= B . A with inner dimension r is not a crude compression forced on the model — it is a faithful match to the shape of the update the task actually wants. LoRA does not prove r is enough for every task; it BETS that it is, parameterises the update as rank r, and lets training confirm or deny the wager. Choose r too small and the correction cannot fit the task; choose it well and a few thousand numbers do the work of a million. The deeper reason the bet pays — that fine-tuning updates have fast-decaying singular values — is the study of a later chamber.

exhibits.title: Frozen, Shared, and Cheap to Keep
exhibits.text:
Freezing W is not a detail — it is the source of every saving. When the great tapestry is frozen, no gradient ever flows into its million threads: there is nothing to differentiate there, nothing to update, nothing to store as a changed copy. The one heavy W is trained ONCE, in the arts below, and thereafter SHARED unchanged by every attunement laid over it.

What is trained, and what is stored, is only the pair A and B — sixteen thousand numbers where there were a million. So every adapted version of the model is not a fresh multi-gigabyte work; it is a tiny adapter, a few megabytes of A and B, resting against the same frozen base. You may keep a hundred such adapters for the cost of keeping one whole model. The expensive thing is made once and never moved; the cheap thing is what you learn, save, and carry. Freeze the base, whisper the delta: that is the economy of the whole workshop.

exhibits.title: The Decomposition of the Update
exhibits.spec:
graph LR
  W["W  d x d  frozen  (1,000,000)"] --> SUM(("+"))
  A["A  r x d  (8,000)"] --> B["B  d x r  (8,000)"]
  B --> BA["B . A  d x d  (16,000 trained)"]
  BA --> SUM
  SUM --> WN["W_new = W + B . A  d x d"]
exhibits.caption: The frozen base W (a million parameters, never updated) is summed with the low-rank product B . A. A squeezes to the inner rank r, B expands back to d, so B . A has the full d x d shape and adds directly onto W. Only the 16,000 numbers of A and B are learned; W_new = W + B . A.

exhibits.title: The Savings Ledger, Drawn to Scale
exhibits.caption: Read the ledger of the wager in three hands. (a) The shapes: the frozen update DELTA-W is a full d x d square — a million threads; beside it, its approximation B . A is drawn true to form. B is d tall but only r wide, A is r tall and d wide, and where they meet the cloth narrows to a waist just r across. A product forced through a waist of r can carry rank no greater than r. (b) The count laid bare: a full DELTA-W is 1,000,000 numbers, while B . A costs only (d x r) + (r x d) = 16,000 — sixty-two times fewer to learn and to keep. (c) The sweep: as the rank r climbs 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, the cost of B . A = 2 d r rises with it, yet even at r = 32 it sits far beneath the flat line of full fine-tuning. At r = 8 the whole correction is 16,000 numbers. Choose r small and a few thousand values do the work of a million — that is the low-rank bet, shown to scale.

exhibits.title: Where the Correction Is Laid
exhibits.text:
LoRA is not smeared across the whole model. The adapter is laid on SPECIFIC weight matrices — most often the attention projections learned in the Attention wing below: W_q, W_k, W_v, and the output projection W_o. Each chosen matrix keeps its frozen W and gains its own parallel pair A and B; the rest of the model is left entirely untouched. Sometimes the MLP weights are adapted too, when the task demands more reach, but the query-key-value-output projections are the standard and usually sufficient target.

This is why the two staircases climb here from Attention and from Diffusion: LoRA does not replace those arts, it attunes them, reaching precisely into their attention machinery. HOW the correction runs beside W without being a layer stacked after it — and how the rank r and the strength are chosen, merged, or plugged in — are the studies of the chambers ahead. (Upstairs of nothing: this is the top of the lineage; every art it adapts lies below.)
